issue.title: Stabilize prompt-catalog event-loop heartbeat test under xdist load
issue.description: During the required just check for runner occupancy history, tests/ace/tui/test_prompt_catalog.py::test_catalog_loading_worker_does_not_block_event_loop failed in the four-worker full suite after 25,378 other tests passed, then passed immediately in isolation and passed in the repeat full just check. The test gives the call_soon heartbeat only 50 ms while all xdist workers are CPU-saturated, so the failure is load-sensitive rather than a deterministic prompt-catalog regression. Reproduce under contention, determine whether the implementation or timing assertion owns the issue, and make the test deterministic without weakening its guarantee that catalog construction stays off the Textual event loop.

payload.close_reason: Backlog triage 2026-08-05: consolidating the full-parallel-suite / xdist flake class onto umbrella task sase-ct ('Flaky ACE TUI tests under full parallel just test run'). Every one of these reports the same shape — a single node fails under the full four-to-27-worker 'just test' or 'just check' run and passes immediately in isolation — so they share a root-cause class (xdist load sensitivity and shared-state leakage across workers) rather than per-test logic bugs. Per-test detail, including sase-cu's pump-free clipboard-task diagnosis, stays readable on each bead, and a +1 with fresh evidence reopens any of them if a specific node turns into a deterministic failure.
